findings.title: [P2] Avoid rebuilding current IDs for every previous item
findings.body: The filter callback at `src/reconcile.ts:41` re-evaluates `current.map(candidate => candidate.id).includes(item.id)` on every element of `previous`. That maps the entire `current` array into a new temporary array and linearly scans it once per previous item, versus the removed one-time `Set` construction with O(1) lookups — an algorithmic drop from O(P+C) to O(P×C) plus O(P) intermediate allocations. The reviewer lane measured ~192 ms vs ~0.94 ms for a 5,000×5,000 element case. Output is unchanged for all inputs, so this is a pure performance regression; it will bite on larger reconciliation batches. Restoring the `Set`-based check (or hoisting the mapped array out of the callback) preserves the new formatting while recovering linear behavior.
